title: Protocol and Vector Again
premise: Ulyana Winterbourne, a clone of the murdered courier Elara Winterbourne, discovers her own name on the manifest of the Meridian, a ship that was destroyed twelve years ago — the night Elara died. The manifest conceals an encrypted message Elara died carrying, one that proves both fleets' high commands engineered the war's opening strike. As the truce expires, Ulyana must choose between delivering the truth, which could shatter the fragile peace and expose her as a clone with no legal identity, and burying it to protect the man she loves, a fleet intelligence officer ordered to erase the message and her. She delivers the message publicly, forcing both commands into open confession, and ends the war at the cost of her old life — walking free only because thousands of crew refuse orders to fire on her ship.
about_author: Odile Whitlock is a former maritime radio operator who spent a decade aboard container vessels before turning to fiction. She writes about people who carry things — cargo, secrets, other people's memories — across distances that should have broken them.

chapters.title: Dead Weight
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Hauling scrap through the contested Kestrel Run, she files a routine manifest and finds the Meridian — a ship that burned twelve years ago, the night the original Elara was murdered — listed as active, with her own name as registered owner. Emotional beat: unease curdling into obsession; the past is not past.

chapters.title: The Ghost in the Ledger
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. She bribes a port archivist and learns the Meridian's registry was reactivated three days ago from a station that no longer exists. Someone is using the dead ship's identity to move something through the truce lines. Emotional beat: the clone's hunger for the original's history, and the first hint that the murder case was never closed.

chapters.title: Manifest Destiny
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Following the ghost manifest, she docks at Verity Station and finds the Meridian physically there, refitted and dark, its cargo bay sealed with fleet intelligence locks. She meets Dain Okafor, an intelligence officer who should arrest her — and who instead warns her to leave. Emotional beat: attraction shadowed by the suspicion he was sent for her.

chapters.title: What Elara Knew
chapters.summary: Alternating POV: Ulyana in the present, recovered memory-fragments from the original Elara. Ulyana breaks into the Meridian's hold and finds a black box keyed to Elara's genome — to hers. The fragments reveal Elara was carrying proof the war's first strike was ordered by both fleets' commands. Emotional beat: inheritance as burden; she is the only key.

chapters.title: Truce Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Dain's POV. Ordered to erase the box and terminate the clone, he falsifies his reports instead, buying Ulyana time while the fleet counts down to the truce's expiry. He tells her the truth about his orders and lets her decide whether to run. Emotional beat: love against duty, chosen explicitly for the first time.

chapters.title: The Long Way Around
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. A chase through debris fields as both fleets hunt the Meridian; Ulyana flies the dead ship herself, using Elara's logged routes. An ambush kills her copilot and forces her to admit the message may end the war — or give both commands an excuse to start it cleanly. Emotional beat: grief hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: Decryption
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Hiding in a neutral shipyard, Ulyana opens the box with Dain's help. The full record names admirals on both sides and includes Elara's final log: she chose to die rather than surrender it, and recorded a message for her clone — for Ulyana — asking her to choose freely. Emotional beat: the original becomes a person, not a template.

chapters.title: Orders of Magnitude
chapters.summary: Dain's POV. His command discovers his deception; he is stripped of rank and ordered to prove loyalty by delivering Ulyana and the box. Instead he transmits the decryption to every crew channel in both fleets, knowing it will cost him everything. Emotional beat: duty redefined — owed to the truth, not the chain of command.

chapters.title: The Meridian Flies
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Climax. With the truce hours from expiry, Ulyana flies the Meridian openly between the two massed fleets, broadcasting Elara's evidence on all bands. Guns track her; crews on both sides refuse firing orders as the truth spreads ship to ship. The commands stand down rather than fire on their own people. Emotional beat: terror transfigured into triumph.

chapters.title: Registered Owner
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Resolution. Tribunals convene; the war ends not in peace but in an armed, wary honesty. Ulyana is legally recognized as a person in her own right — registered owner of the Meridian at last, the manifest corrected. She and Dain, both stripped of their old lives, take a cargo contract together. Emotional beat: inheritance resolved — she keeps the name, but it is hers now.
